title: Cube & Dice
summary: Dice questions ask for opposite faces from several positions (adjacent-four, two-common-faces and same-position rules), or from an unfolded net (skip one; ends of a Z). Painted-cube questions use 8, 12(n−2), 6(n−2)² and (n−2)³.

subtopics.title: Dice: finding opposite faces from positions
subtopics.concept:
A die (cube) has 6 faces: each face touches 4 others and is **opposite** exactly 1. When several views of the same die are shown, use these rules:

1. **Adjacent-four rule** — a face seen next to four different faces is opposite the sixth one.
2. **Two common faces** — if two views share two faces, the remaining face in each view is opposite the other one.
3. **Same position** — if one face is common and it sits in the **same position** in both views, the faces in matching positions are opposite (front ↔ front, right ↔ right).
4. **Never together** — two faces seen together in any view can never be opposite.

A **standard die** has opposite faces summing to 7: (1, 6), (2, 5), (3, 4).

formulas.name: Standard die
formulas.note: Opposite faces of a standard die.

tricks.title: Eliminate the neighbours
tricks.body: List every face seen with the asked face; strike them out. If only one face is left, it is the answer — no rotation needed.

example.q: **Q.** 4 is seen with 1, 2, 3 and 5. What is opposite 4?
example.solution: Only 6 is never seen with 4, so **6**.

tricks.title: Two common faces
tricks.body: Two views sharing two faces: the leftover faces are opposite.

example.q: **Q.** Views show (A, B, C) and (A, B, D). Opposite of C?
example.solution: A and B are common, so **D**.

mistakes: Declaring two faces opposite just because they never appear together — check that the other four are all ruled out.
Applying the same-position rule when the common face is in different positions.
Forgetting that a standard-die fact (sum 7) only holds when the question says the die is standard.

subtopics.title: Cube nets: folding a sheet into a cube
subtopics.concept:
An open (unfolded) cube is a **net** of 6 squares. To find opposite faces without folding mentally:

- In any straight row or column, faces with **exactly one square between them** are opposite.
- In a **Z (or S) shape** of four squares, the two end squares are opposite.
- Two squares that touch along an edge in the net are always adjacent on the cube.

To test whether a drawn cube can be made: first reject any cube that shows two opposite faces together; then check the order of the three visible faces around their shared corner.

tricks.title: Skip one
tricks.body: Along a line of squares, skip one: 1st ↔ 3rd, 2nd ↔ 4th.

example.q: **Q.** Row A B C D in a net. Opposite of B?

mistakes: Treating squares that only meet at a corner in the net as opposite.
Accepting a cube that shows two faces which are opposite in the net.
Ignoring the order (clockwise/anticlockwise) of the three visible faces.

subtopics.title: Painted cube cut into small cubes
subtopics.concept:
A cube of side n painted on all faces and cut into n³ unit cubes gives:

- 3 faces painted: the 8 corner cubes
- 2 faces painted: edge cubes, 12(n − 2)
- 1 face painted: face centres, 6(n − 2)²
- no face painted: the inner core, (n − 2)³

For a cuboid a × b × c, think the same way: corners 8, edges 4[(a−2)+(b−2)+(c−2)], faces 2[(a−2)(b−2)+(b−2)(c−2)+(c−2)(a−2)], core (a−2)(b−2)(c−2) (when every side is at least 2).

formulas.name: Two faces painted
formulas.note: Cubes on the edges, excluding corners.

formulas.name: One face painted
formulas.note: Cubes in the middle of each face.

tricks.title: Check the total
tricks.body: 8 + 12(n−2) + 6(n−2)² + (n−2)³ = n³. Use it to verify your counts.

mistakes: Using n instead of (n − 2) in the formulas.
Forgetting that corner cubes always have 3 painted faces, whatever n is.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Two or three drawings of the same die; ask the face opposite to X.
pyqPatterns.approach: Adjacent-four rule, two-common-faces rule, or same-position rule.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: The die is stated to be standard / ordinary.
An unfolded sheet with 6 labelled squares.
pyqPatterns.approach: Skip-one in a line; ends of a Z are opposite.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Net in the question, four cubes in the options.
pyqPatterns.approach: Reject cubes showing an opposite pair; then check the corner order.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Cube painted and cut into n³ small cubes.

solvedExamples.solution: Face 1 is common to both views and sits in the **same position** (top). So faces in matching positions are opposite: the front faces 2 and 5 are opposite (and so are the right faces 3 and 4). Opposite of 2 is **5**.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Common face in the same place → match the other positions.

solvedExamples.solution: Opposite pairs from the net: K–O and M–J (skip one in the column K, M, O, J) and L–N (skip one in the row L, M, N). The cube with K and O together and the one with J and M together are impossible. Of the two left, fold the net with M facing you: K folds up to the top and N folds to the right, which is exactly the cube with K on top, M in front and N on the right. The cube with N in front and M on the right has the same three faces but in the reverse order around the corner, so it cannot be formed.
solvedExamples.shortcut: First strike out cubes showing an opposite pair.

solvedExamples.q: A cube of side 4 cm is painted red on all its faces and then cut into small cubes of side 1 cm. How many small cubes have **exactly two** faces painted?
solvedExamples.solution: n = 4. Cubes with exactly two painted faces lie along the 12 edges, excluding the corners: each edge has n − 2 = 2 of them. Total 12 × 2 = **24**.

practice.shortcut: Same position of the common face.

practice.solution: 3 appears with 1 and 2 in the first view and with 6 and 4 in the second. So 3 is adjacent to 1, 2, 4 and 6; the only remaining face, **5**, is opposite 3.

practice.q: An ordinary die, whose opposite faces always add up to 7, shows 2 on top, 6 in front and 4 on the right. What is the sum of the numbers on the bottom, back and left faces?
practice.solution: Opposite faces add to 7: bottom = 7 − 2 = 5, back = 7 − 6 = 1, left = 7 − 4 = 3. Sum = 5 + 1 + 3 = **9**.

practice.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which face will be opposite to the face showing **Q**? (Ignore the orientation of the letters/numbers.)
practice.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 102 78" width="102" height="78" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="3,3 27,3 27,27 3,27"/><text x="15" y="20" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">P</text><polygon points="27,3 51,3 51,27 27,27"/><text x="39" y="20" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">Q</text><polygon points="27,27 51,27 51,51 27,51"/><text x="39" y="44" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">R</text><polygon points="51,27 75,27 75,51 51,51"/><text x="63" y="44" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">S</text><polygon points="51,51 75,51 75,75 51,75"/><text x="63" y="68" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">T</text><polygon points="75,51 99,51 99,75 75,75"/><text x="87" y="68" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">U</text></svg>
practice.solution: The net is a staircase. Q, R, S, T form a Z shape of four squares, and the end squares of a Z are opposite: Q ↔ T. (Similarly P ↔ S and R ↔ U.) Answer **T**.
practice.shortcut: Ends of a Z are opposite.

practice.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which face will be opposite to the face showing **2**? (Ignore the orientation of the letters/numbers.)
practice.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 126 54" width="126" height="54" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="3,3 27,3 27,27 3,27"/><text x="15" y="20" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">1</text><polygon points="27,3 51,3 51,27 27,27"/><text x="39" y="20" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">2</text><polygon points="51,3 75,3 75,27 51,27"/><text x="63" y="20" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">3</text><polygon points="51,27 75,27 75,51 51,51"/><text x="63" y="44" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">4</text><polygon points="75,27 99,27 99,51 75,51"/><text x="87" y="44" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">5</text><polygon points="99,27 123,27 123,51 99,51"/><text x="111" y="44" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">6</text></svg>
practice.solution: Rows of three: 1 ↔ 3 (skip 2) and 4 ↔ 6 (skip 5). The remaining two faces, 2 and 5, are opposite (they are also the ends of the Z formed by 2, 3, 4, 5). Answer **5**.
practice.shortcut: Pair the rows first; the leftovers pair up.

practice.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which pair of letters will be on **opposite** faces? (Ignore the orientation of the letters/numbers.)
practice.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 78 102" width="78" height="102" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="27,3 51,3 51,27 27,27"/><text x="39" y="20" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">K</text><polygon points="3,27 27,27 27,51 3,51"/><text x="15" y="44" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">L</text><polygon points="27,27 51,27 51,51 27,51"/><text x="39" y="44" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">M</text><polygon points="51,27 75,27 75,51 51,51"/><text x="63" y="44" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">N</text><polygon points="27,51 51,51 51,75 27,75"/><text x="39" y="68" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">O</text><polygon points="27,75 51,75 51,99 27,99"/><text x="39" y="92" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">J</text></svg>
practice.solution: In the column K, M, O, J skip one square: K ↔ O and M ↔ J. In the row L, M, N: L ↔ N. So **M and J** are opposite. K and M, L and O, N and J all share an edge in the net or after folding, so they are adjacent.

practice.solution: Opposite pairs: in the row 2, 3, 4, 5 → 2 ↔ 4 and 3 ↔ 5; the leftovers 1 ↔ 6. So a cube showing 1 with 6, or 2 with 4, is impossible. Between the two cubes with 1, 3, 4: fold with 3 facing you — 1 (attached above 2, which folds to the left) comes over the top, and 4 folds to the right. So 1 on top, 3 in front, 4 on the right is correct; the version with 4 in front and 3 on the right has the reverse order.
practice.shortcut: Reject opposite pairs first, then check the corner order.

practice.solution: Opposite pairs: A ↔ C (row A, B, C) and B ↔ E, D ↔ F (column B, D, E, F). So cubes showing A with C or B with E are impossible. With D facing you and B folded over the top, C (to the right of B in the net) comes down on the right side and A on the left. So B top, D front, C right is correct; B top, D front, A right is its mirror and cannot be formed.
practice.shortcut: Opposite pairs out; then fold around the front face.

practice.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **exactly one** face painted?
practice.solution: Each face has a (5 − 2) × (5 − 2) = 9 block of cubes with only that face painted. 6 faces × 9 = **54**.

practice.q: A cube of side 6 units is painted on all faces and then cut into 216 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have **no** face painted?
practice.solution: Remove the outer layer on every side: the unpainted core is (6 − 2)³ = 4³ = **64**.

practice.q: A cuboid 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **exactly two** faces painted?
practice.solution: Two-face cubes lie on the edges, excluding corners. There are 4 edges of each length: 4 × (5 − 2) + 4 × (4 − 2) + 4 × (3 − 2) = 12 + 8 + 4 = **24**.
